design_detail: Systematic review without meta-analysis of prospective cohort studies reporting mortality among people with problematic or dependent cocaine use, done for the Global Burden of Disease Expert Group on Mental Disorders and Illicit Drug Use. EMBASE, Medline and PsycINFO searched for publications from 1990 to 2008, with grey literature, reference lists of reviews, an expert group and unpublished data requested from cohort investigators. Nine cohorts were found and seven gave mortality estimates (USA 2, Canada, France, the Netherlands, Brazil, Italy). Crude mortality rates (CMR) per 100 person-years were taken or recalculated from deaths and person-years; standardized mortality ratios (SMR) were taken as reported (four cohorts); causes of death are described for four cohorts. Estimates were deliberately not pooled.
can_establish: Which cohort studies of mortality in people with problematic or dependent cocaine use had been reported up to 2008, and the range of their crude mortality rates (about 0.5 to 6.2 per 100 person-years) and of the four reported SMRs (about 4.4 to 7.7 against the general population of the same age and sex), with the leading causes of death in four cohorts.
cannot_establish: A pooled or typical mortality rate for people who use cocaine (no pooling, heterogeneous cohorts); mortality among people who use cocaine without injecting, treatment or arrest, since no cohort followed people who only snort cocaine; how much of the excess is due to cocaine itself rather than injecting, HIV, heroin and alcohol use and social disadvantage, since SMRs standardize only for age and sex; or mortality after the cohorts' follow-up periods (1985-2005).

sample.recruitment: Database search (EMBASE, Medline, PsycINFO) for publications from 1990 to 2008 with librarian-designed strings; grey literature through online and library databases; reference lists of review articles; an expert group asked for missed studies; cohort investigators asked for additional data, several of which are cited as personal communications from September to November 2008 (pp. 89-92; Table 1 note, p. 91).
sample.inclusion_exclusion: Included: cohort studies reporting raw data on mortality related to problematic use of or dependence on cocaine. Excluded: not a cohort study, no report of mortality among people using cocaine, no primary data, or case reports of cocaine-related deaths without a denominator (p. 89, 2.2 and 2.3); the flowchart also excludes a wrong time period, before 1990 (Fig. 1, p. 90). Non-English abstracts were screened; one Spanish article contributed data and 14 non-English articles were excluded, none reporting cohort mortality (p. 90, Results, 1st paragraph).
sample.demographics: Cohorts (Table 1, p. 91; pp. 92-93): Brazil 1992-1999, 131 people in treatment for crack dependence; Canada (VIDUS) 1996-2004, 717 people injecting cocaine only; the Netherlands 1985-1993, a subsample of HIV-negative people mainly injecting cocaine within a cohort of 632; USA (RAVEN, Seattle) 1994-1997, 319 injecting cocaine daily and 52 smoking crack daily (overlapping); USA (ALIVE, Baltimore) 1988-2005, 518 injecting cocaine only and 2439 injecting cocaine and heroin, 25% HIV-positive at baseline; France 1992-1999, 2212 people arrested for cocaine or crack use or dealing, mean age 27 at baseline; Italy (Bologna) 1989-2004, 347 people in treatment for cocaine dependence, mostly intranasal, 309 of them men.
sample.attrition: Not reported for most cohorts. Brazil: 70% followed at 12 years, with 4 further deaths not used because no person-years were reported. The excluded Dutch cohort lost 61 of 160 (Table 1, p. 91; p. 92).
sample.selection_effects: All cohorts were recruited through injecting-drug-use research, treatment or arrest, mostly from socially disadvantaged settings and several with high HIV prevalence; none followed people who only snort cocaine (p. 93, 4.1). Five cohorts are from North America or Western Europe, one from Brazil. Several estimates come from personal communications rather than published reports.

exposure.measurement: As defined in each cohort at baseline: primary drug injected, daily injecting or crack smoking, treatment for cocaine dependence, or arrest for cocaine use or dealing; the review calls all of these problematic or dependent cocaine use (p. 90, Results, 4th paragraph). Changes in drug, route or frequency during follow-up were not captured (p. 94).
exposure.dose_frequency_duration_route: Route differed between cohorts: injection (Canada, the Netherlands, ALIVE, RAVEN), crack smoking (Brazil; RAVEN daily non-injecting group), mostly intranasal (Italy), not stated (France). Frequency: daily injecting in RAVEN and ALIVE.
exposure.polysubstance: Not handled at review level. The largest ALIVE group injected heroin as well as cocaine; in Italy concomitant alcohol problems were associated with mortality (p. 92); other drug use is not reported for most cohorts.

comparison.controls: The general population of the same age and sex in each country (SMRs, four cohorts); otherwise none. Within cohorts: people injecting cocaine only against cocaine and heroin (ALIVE), and HIV-positive against HIV-negative people (VIDUS, ALIVE).
comparison.matching: SMRs standardize for age and sex only; CMRs are unadjusted by definition (p. 90, 3.1).
comparison.unmeasured_premorbid: Social disadvantage, HIV infection, injecting, heroin and alcohol use, access to health care and exposure to violence are named by the authors as possible reasons for the differences and were not adjusted for (pp. 93-94).
comparison.controls_other_drug_use: The general-population comparators include people who use drugs; not discussed.

outcomes.instruments: All-cause mortality: CMR per 100 person-years, taken as reported or calculated from deaths and person-years; where only deaths and total years of follow-up were reported, deaths were assumed to occur halfway through follow-up; SMRs as reported; two studies gave only case fatality (p. 90, 2.5, 1st and 2nd paragraphs). Causes of death: counts and percentages (Table 2) or cause-specific SMRs.
outcomes.validity_norms: How deaths were identified in each cohort (linkage to death registers, death certificates, contact with families or services) and who assigned the causes are not reported; cause categories differ between cohorts (Table 2 footnotes, p. 92). The authors recommend classifying causes with agreed definitions (p. 94).
outcomes.operationalization: CMR: deaths per 100 person-years of follow-up. SMR: observed deaths divided by those expected for people of the same age and sex in the general population of that country (p. 90, 2.5).
outcomes.multiplicity_correction: Not applicable: descriptive review; the only tests quoted are the cohorts' own HIV comparisons.
outcomes.assessor_blinding: Not applicable. Screening by two researchers independently, with shortlists compared and resolved by consensus; extraction by two researchers, compared for consistency (p. 89, 2.1 and 2.4).

analysis.effect_sizes: No pooled estimate. CMR per 100 person-years (Table 1, p. 91): Canada VIDUS 6.16 (95% CI 5.21 to 7.11; 161 deaths, 2613.2 person-years); ALIVE cocaine only 4.69 (4.03 to 5.45; 175 deaths, 3727 person-years); ALIVE cocaine and heroin 4.37 (4.07 to 4.68; 787 deaths, 18,023 person-years); the Netherlands 4.6 (9 deaths, 194 person-years); Brazil 3.51 (23 deaths); RAVEN daily crack smoking 3.53 (3 deaths, 85 person-years) and daily injecting 0.53 (0.10 to 1.58); France 0.69 (0.55 to 0.87; 80 deaths, 11,496 person-years); Italy 0.54 in men and 0.50 (0.22 to 0.91) in total (7 deaths, all men, 1289 person-years). SMRs: Brazil 7.60; France 4.36 (men) and 7.70 (women); Canada 4.74 (4.19 to 5.29); Italy 4.75 in men (2.26 to 9.96) (p. 92; Table 1). By HIV status: VIDUS 9.83 (7.59 to 12.54) vs 4.91 (3.98 to 5.99), p < .001; ALIVE 7.74 and 7.98 (HIV-positive, cocaine and heroin; cocaine only) vs 3.25 and 3.45 (HIV-negative) (p. 92). Editors' checks of Table 1 against its own deaths and person-years are listed under reporting issues.
analysis.preregistration_detail: The abstract says searches and extraction were undertaken using protocols; no registered or published protocol is cited.
analysis.selective_reporting: The quality index (adapted from McGrath et al., 2004) is described only in Appendix D (not available); Table 1 prints scores from 1 to 15 without the scale's range, and the Italian cohort has no score. Key figures for the Canadian, US (ALIVE) and French cohorts rest on unpublished personal communications.
analysis.power: Not applicable. Several estimates rest on few deaths: 3 in each RAVEN group, 7 in Italy, 9 in the Netherlands.

interpretation_gap.results_show: Seven cohorts of people injecting cocaine, smoking crack, in treatment for cocaine dependence or arrested for cocaine offences reported crude mortality rates of about 0.5 to 6.2 per 100 person-years and, in four of them, SMRs of about 4.4 to 7.7 against the general population of the same age and sex. In the two cohorts of people who inject drugs the commonest causes of death were AIDS, overdose and trauma; in the Brazilian crack cohort, gunshot wounds and AIDS.
interpretation_gap.claimed: The abstract says the SMRs suggest mortality four to eight times higher among people who use cocaine than in age and sex peers (p. 88). The Discussion itself calls this an extremely crude summary (p. 93) and the limitations explain why it cannot be generalized to all people with cocaine dependence, still less to all who use cocaine (p. 93); the abstract's conclusion about uncertain generalizability is appropriately cautious. Remaining gaps: the abstract does not say that the SMR cohorts were injecting, treatment or arrestee samples with high HIV prevalence and heavy heroin use, so the 4-8 figure cannot be read as an effect of cocaine; the CMR range differs between abstract (0.53 to 6.16), table (from 0.50) and Discussion (0.48 to 6.16); and the Italian SMR is 4.75 in the Results and 4.6 in the Discussion.

timeline.event: Van Haastrecht et al.: Amsterdam cohort of people who use drugs (included; 4.6 deaths per 100 person-years among HIV-negative people mainly injecting cocaine).
Ribeiro et al.: São Paulo cohort of 131 people treated for crack dependence (included; SMR 7.6 at 5 years); OFDT French national cohort of people arrested for cocaine or crack (included).
Wang et al.: ALIVE cohort, Baltimore, on HIV infection and overdose mortality (included; cause-of-death data supplied by personal communication).
Pavarin: Bologna cohort of 347 people in treatment for cocaine dependence (included; SMR 4.75 in men).
Arendt et al.: Danish nationwide follow-up of people treated for cocaine and other drug use disorders; on the project's cocaine list, not yet read (title only).
This review: the first systematic review of prospective studies of mortality in problematic or dependent cocaine use, by the authors' account (p. 89).

Pavarin: follow-up of 178 people treated for crack problems; van Amsterdam et al.: systematic review of mortality in people who use both opioids and cocaine compared with opioids only; both on the project's cocaine list, not yet read (titles only).

replication.where_it_stands: The review documents how thin the cohort evidence on cocaine mortality was up to 2008: seven heterogeneous cohorts, four SMRs, several figures from personal communications. Its 4-8 SMR range should be cited only for the populations studied. Later cohorts and reviews on the project's list must be appraised before the encyclopedia states a current figure.

funding.funder: National Drug and Alcohol Research Centre, University of NSW, Australia; L. Degenhardt holds an Australian NHMRC Senior Research Fellowship (p. 94, Role of funding source).
funding.affiliations_note: Completed as part of work for the Global Burden of Disease Expert Group on Mental Disorders and Illicit Drug Use (p. 94, Acknowledgements). Co-author T. Kerr (British Columbia Centre for Excellence in HIV/AIDS) supplied the VIDUS estimates by personal communication (p. 92; Table 1 note); co-authors S. Mehta and G. Kirk are at the Johns Hopkins School of Public Health, from where the ALIVE data were supplied by personal communication (pp. 92, 94). No procedure for appraising data from co-authors' own cohorts is described. Recorded as a flag, not a reason to discount.

what_would_settle_it: Record-linkage cohorts of people whose main drug is cocaine, drawn from treatment services, arrest records, emergency departments and harm-reduction services and including people who snort cocaine, followed through national death registers, reporting person-years, SMRs by age, sex and route, and cause-specific mortality adjusted for injecting, HIV, opioid and alcohol use and socio-economic position; then a pooled analysis of such cohorts.

domains.domain: 1. PICO components in research question and inclusion criteria
domains.note: Population (problematic or dependent cocaine use), cohort design, comparator for excess mortality (general population via SMR) and outcomes (crude, excess and cause-specific mortality, mortality by HIV status) are stated (p. 89).
The abstract mentions protocols, but no registered or published protocol is cited and its content is not described.
The Introduction explains why prospective cohorts rather than poisoning registers or post-mortem series were chosen (p. 89).

Three databases, grey literature, reference lists, an expert group and contact with investigators, which would otherwise merit at least partial yes; but publications were limited to 1990-2008 and a wrong time period (before 1990) was an exclusion reason, without justification. Applied as written, as for other cards of this project (decision p-amstar2-item4 pending with the senior author).
Two researchers independently compiled shortlists, compared and resolved by consensus (p. 89, 2.1).
Two researchers extracted data and compared results, resolving differences by consensus (p. 89, 2.4).

domains.domain: 7. List of excluded studies with justification (critical)
domains.note: Exclusions are given as category counts in Fig. 1; only the two cohort studies excluded at the last step are named with reasons (Table 1b).

domains.domain: 8. Included studies described in adequate detail
domains.note: Table 1 gives country, years, sample type, N, person-years, deaths, CMR and SMR; age, sex, HIV prevalence, follow-up length and ascertainment of deaths are missing for most cohorts.

domains.domain: 9. Satisfactory risk-of-bias assessment of included studies (critical)
domains.note: A quality index adapted from McGrath et al. (2004) was scored, but its criteria are only in Appendix D, which was not available; the main text gives a total score without range or domains, and none for the Italian cohort.

domains.domain: 10. Funding sources of included studies reported

domains.note: No pooling, explicitly justified by the few and heterogeneous cohorts (p. 90, 2.5).

domains.domain: 12. Impact of risk of bias on pooled results assessed
13. Risk of bias accounted for in interpretation (critical)
domains.note: The limitations discuss selection of injecting and treatment samples, HIV, geography, social disadvantage and baseline-only exposure definitions as reasons the estimates may not generalize (pp. 93-94).
Differences in CMR are discussed in terms of general health, route, HIV, access to care and disadvantage, with the authors stating they cannot tell which factors contribute (p. 93).

domains.domain: 16. Conflicts of interest and funding reported
domains.note: Funding and a declaration of no conflicts are given; the involvement of co-authors in included cohorts is not flagged.

risk_of_bias.reasoning: Provisional: item 9 can only be judged from Appendix D, which was not read, but the overall rating does not depend on it. Three critical items are not met (no registered protocol, an unexplained limit on publication years, no list of excluded studies), which gives critically low confidence under AMSTAR 2; even with items 2 and 4 read leniently, item 7 alone would give low confidence. The rating concerns whether the review can be trusted to have found and fairly summarized every cohort; it does not mean its figures are wrong. The review is transparent about its limits and does not pool. Its numbers are second-hand: several come from personal communications, and Table 1 has internal inconsistencies (reporting issues). Cite for: the range of crude mortality rates and the four SMRs reported by cohorts of people who inject cocaine, smoke crack, are in treatment or were arrested (data 1985-2005), and their leading causes of death. Do not cite for: the mortality of people who use cocaine in general, or for an effect of cocaine itself.

key_findings.finding: Flowchart: 1911 database records plus 4 from reference lists; after excluding 1167 not about cocaine and 452 not about mortality associated with cocaine use, 296 remained; after further exclusions and 3 expert-group and 2 grey-literature additions, 64 papers were extracted and 9 papers on 7 cohort studies gave usable mortality data.
key_findings.note: The Results text gives different counts for the same steps (see reporting issues).

key_findings.finding: Nine cohort studies since 1990 included people who use cocaine; seven gave mortality estimates (USA 2, Canada, France, the Netherlands, Brazil, Italy). Two were excluded for insufficient data: a Dutch cohort of 160 with 61 lost to follow-up, and a UK treatment cohort of 1075 (247 with cocaine dependence) that did not report deaths among them.
key_findings.locator: Results, 3rd paragraph (p. 90); Table 1b (p. 91); 3.1 All-cause mortality, 9th paragraph (p. 92)

key_findings.finding: Crude mortality rates per 100 person-years: Canada (VIDUS, 717 people injecting cocaine only) 6.16 (5.21 to 7.11), 161 deaths in 2613.2 person-years; ALIVE cocaine only 4.69 (4.03 to 5.45), 175 deaths in 3727 person-years; ALIVE cocaine and heroin 4.37 (4.07 to 4.68), 787 deaths in 18,023 person-years; the Netherlands 4.6 (9 deaths, 194 person-years); Brazil 3.51 (23 deaths among 131); RAVEN daily crack smoking 3.53 (3 deaths, 85 person-years) and daily injecting 0.53 (0.10 to 1.58); France 0.69 (0.55 to 0.87), 80 deaths in 11,496 person-years; Italy 0.54 in men and 0.50 (0.22 to 0.91) overall, 7 deaths, all in men.
key_findings.note: Three rows do not agree with their own deaths and person-years (RAVEN daily injecting, Italy, Brazil); see reporting issues.

key_findings.finding: SMRs against the general population of the same age and sex were reported by four cohorts: Brazil 7.6 at 5-year follow-up; France 4.36 in men and 7.70 in women; Canada 4.74 (4.19 to 5.29); Italy 4.75 in men (2.26 to 9.96).

Mortality by HIV status: in VIDUS 9.83 per 100 person-years (7.59 to 12.54) among HIV-positive and 4.91 (3.98 to 5.99) among HIV-negative people injecting cocaine (p < .001); in ALIVE, where 25% were HIV-positive at baseline, 7.74 and 7.98 among HIV-positive people (cocaine and heroin; cocaine only) and 3.25 and 3.45 among HIV-negative people.

Causes of death: in the Brazilian crack treatment cohort, gunshot wounds 10 of 23 deaths (44%) and AIDS-related illness 6 (26%); in the Italian cohort's 309 men, cause-specific SMRs of 14.85 (4.79 to 46.04) for vascular diseases, 7.07 (1 to 50.16) for suicide and 9.95 (1.40 to 70.61) for overdose.

ALIVE causes of death (Table 2): people injecting cocaine and heroin, AIDS 206 of 787 deaths (26.2%), overdose 134 (17.0%), sepsis or endocarditis 81 (10.3%), traumatic deaths 60 (7.6%), cardiac 54 (6.9%), suicide 3 (0.4%); people injecting cocaine only, AIDS 62 of 175 (35.4%), overdose 20 (11.4%), sepsis or endocarditis 15 (8.6%), traumatic 12 (6.9%), cardiac 7 (4.0%), suicide 2 (1.1%).

VIDUS causes of death (Table 2): overdose 53, AIDS 30, traumatic deaths 23, suicide 7, cardiac 6 and sepsis or endocarditis 5 of 158 deaths; the text reports overdose 35%, HIV and AIDS 20% and traumatic deaths 15% as the commonest.
key_findings.note: The printed percentages use a denominator of 150 (with 158 they are 33.5%, 19.0% and 14.6%; editors' arithmetic); see reporting issues.

key_findings.finding: The authors summarize the SMRs, extremely crudely in their words, as deaths occurring four to eight times more often than in the general population of the same age and sex, and attribute differences in CMR to general health, route, HIV, access to care and possibly disadvantage, without being able to say which.

Limitations stated by the authors: most cohorts were people injecting cocaine daily or with crack dependence, mostly from socially disadvantaged settings; no study followed people who only snort cocaine; HIV was highly prevalent in several cohorts and the effect of antiretroviral treatment could not be examined; drug use was defined at baseline only.

No pooled estimates were made because of the few studies, the varied populations and the limited statistics reported; where only deaths and total years of follow-up were reported, CMRs were approximated by assuming deaths occurred halfway through follow-up.
key_findings.locator: 2.5 Reporting of mortality estimates, 2nd and 3rd paragraphs

reporting_issues.issue: The study flow cannot be reconciled: the text gives 1917 articles, 1160 excluded as not about cocaine, 71 studies remaining and 10 articles or reports on nine cohorts; Fig. 1 gives 1911 plus 4 records, 1167 excluded as not about cocaine, 64 papers extracted and 9 papers on 7 cohorts; and the text's own exclusions (1160, 452, 151, 32, 23, 17) leave 82, not 71 (editors' arithmetic).
reporting_issues.consequence: The number of studies screened and excluded at each step is uncertain; this weakens the audit trail behind AMSTAR 2 items 4 and 7.

reporting_issues.issue: The range of crude mortality rates is given as 0.53 to 6.16 in the abstract and 0.48 to 6.16 in the Discussion, while the lowest value in Table 1 is 0.50 (Italy, total).
reporting_issues.consequence: Cite the range from Table 1 (about 0.5 to 6.2 per 100 person-years).

reporting_issues.issue: The Italian SMR in men is 4.75 (2.26 to 9.96) in Table 1 and the Results but 4.6 in the Discussion.
reporting_issues.consequence: Minor; the table value should be used.

reporting_issues.issue: The French cohort is 2212 people in Table 1 and 2122 in the text.
reporting_issues.consequence: Minor transcription error; the CMR (80 deaths in 11,496 person-years) is unaffected.

reporting_issues.issue: VIDUS deaths are 161 in Table 1 and the text, 158 in Table 2 (whose counts sum to 158) and in Fig. 2, while Table 2's VIDUS percentages correspond to a denominator of 150 and sum to 105.3% (editors' arithmetic); Fig. 2 plots shares out of 158 (AIDS about 19%).
reporting_issues.consequence: The VIDUS cause-of-death percentages should be recalculated from the counts (overdose 33.5%, AIDS 19.0%, traumatic 14.6% of 158) before citation.

reporting_issues.issue: RAVEN daily injecting group: 3 deaths in 319 person-years gives 0.94 per 100 person-years (exact 95% CI 0.19 to 2.75; editors' calculation), not the printed 0.53 (0.10 to 1.58), which would fit about 566 person-years; a footnote says the same 3 deaths are counted in both RAVEN groups.
reporting_issues.consequence: The lowest CMR in the abstract (0.53) is itself in doubt.

reporting_issues.issue: Italian row: 7 deaths in 1289 person-years gives 0.54 per 100 person-years, which the table prints as the men's rate, while the total is printed as 0.50; with all 7 deaths in men, the men's rate must exceed the total, so the 1289 person-years appear to be the men's only (editors' arithmetic). The men's CI (0.00 to 1.07) is also a symmetric approximation that reaches zero.
reporting_issues.consequence: The Italian person-years and rates cannot be taken from the table without checking the primary report.

reporting_issues.issue: Brazilian row: no person-years are given; the CMR of 3.51 equals 23 deaths over 655 person-years, that is 131 people times 5 years, counting full follow-up for those who died; the review's stated mid-point method would give about 3.85 and the 44.3-month average follow-up in the table about 4.8 (editors' arithmetic).
reporting_issues.consequence: The Brazilian CMR may be underestimated; the method used for it is not the one described.

reporting_issues.issue: Table 1 labels the ALIVE cohort as HIV-seronegative people who inject drugs, but the text says 25% were HIV-positive at baseline and reports CMRs for HIV-positive participants, and AIDS is the leading cause of death in Table 2.
reporting_issues.consequence: The table label is wrong; the ALIVE estimates include HIV-positive people.

reporting_issues.issue: In the Netherlands row, N = 632 is the whole cohort, while the 9 deaths and 194 person-years refer to the HIV-negative subsample mainly injecting cocaine, whose size is not given.
reporting_issues.consequence: The number of people behind the Dutch CMR is unknown.

reporting_issues.issue: The text refers to Table 4 for the ALIVE causes of death; the paper has two tables (Table 2 is meant). The Italian cohort is described as non-injecting people dependent on crack (p. 90) and elsewhere as mostly intranasal (pp. 92-93). Table 1 has no caption, and the method for the 95% CIs of cause-of-death shares in Table 2 is not given (they are wider than binomial intervals: 62 of 175 gives about 28% to 43%, printed 24.4% to 46.4%).
reporting_issues.consequence: Minor reporting errors that make the tables harder to audit.
